import numpy as np,json
r=d[d.valve=='R'];x=r.length_mm.values;y=r.height_mm.values
c=np.corrcoef(x,y)[0,1];s=np.sign(c)*y.std(ddof=1)/x.std(ddof=1);i=y.mean()-s*x.mean()
print(s,i,len(x))
ex=[{"id":k,"reason":"left valve of an individual already represented by its right valve (duplicate measurement)"} for k in d.specimen[d.valve=='L']]
json.dump({"status":"completed","results":{"slope":float(s),"intercept":float(i),"n":int(len(x))},
"assumptions":["Left valves are duplicates of the same individuals as their right valves; individuals = right valves."],
"exclusions":ex,"issues":["4 individuals were catalogued twice (R and L valves with identical measurements), which would pseudo-replicate the fit."],
"summary":"RMA regression (slope = sign(r)*sd_y/sd_x, intercept = mean_y - slope*mean_x) of height on length using the 30 right valves, one per individual."},open('answer.json','w'),indent=1)

import numpy as np,json,pandas as pd
d=pd.read_csv('valves.csv')
r=d[d.valve=='R'];x=r.length_mm.values;y=r.height_mm.values
c=np.corrcoef(x,y)[0,1];s=np.sign(c)*y.std(ddof=1)/x.std(ddof=1);i=y.mean()-s*x.mean()
print(s,i,len(x))
ex=[{"id":k,"reason":"left valve of an individual already represented by its right valve (duplicate measurement)"} for k in d.specimen[d.valve=='L']]
json.dump({"status":"completed","results":{"slope":float(s),"intercept":float(i),"n":int(len(x))},
"assumptions":["Left valves are duplicates of the same individuals as their right valves; individuals = right valves."],
"exclusions":ex,"issues":["4 individuals were catalogued twice (R and L valves with identical measurements), which would pseudo-replicate the fit."],
"summary":"RMA regression (slope = sign(r)*sd_y/sd_x, intercept = mean_y - slope*mean_x) of height on length using the 30 right valves, one per individual."},open('answer.json','w'),indent=1)

content.text:
I fitted the reduced major axis regression of height on length and wrote `answer.json`. The fit gives a slope of 0.7662579850472728, an intercept of −0.8346781441373174 and n = 30.

`valves.csv` had 34 rows. Four of them (V01L, V12L, V16L and V20L) are left valves of individuals whose right valves were also catalogued. Their measurements are identical to the right valves, so keeping them would have counted those individuals twice. I dropped them and used the 30 right valves, one per individual. The exclusions are listed in `answer.json`.

I computed the slope as the standard deviation of height divided by the standard deviation of length, with the sign of the correlation. The intercept is mean height minus slope times mean length. The status is "completed", and the one assumption, that each left valve belongs to the same individual as its matching right valve, is recorded in the file.
